summary_paragraph: A woman with systemic lupus erythematosus, chronic abdominal pain, and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome was admitted after presenting with low-grade fever, tachycardia, and recurrence of abdominal pain following three weeks of pain relief on weekly steroid injections. She had no signs of active infection, pancreatitis, or other acute pathology. Labs were stable, and no imaging was performed due to prior extensive radiation exposure. Her symptoms improved with IV fluids, analgesia, and anti-nausea treatment. After reassessment and patient request, she was discharged home within 12 hours with stable vital signs, a negative workup, and instructions to resume her outpatient lupus and POTS regimens.
problems: Intestinal infection due to other organism, not elsewhere classified
